There have long been rumours that Apple is preparing a brand-new iPhone with an all-glass design to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the iPhone next year. However, an analyst at Jefferies believes that the device will no longer be moving forward.

Wall Street analyst says bold iPhone 20th-anniversary redesign plans have been cancelled

Wall Street investment bank Jefferies today downgraded Apple's stock rating to "underperform," with analyst Edison Lee (李) noting that the potential cancellation of the iPhone 20th-anniversary redesign is one of the main reasons.

The key to this downgrade lies in doubts that Apple's all-glass iPhone plans have fallen through. Although the project was reported to be under development as early as 2025, with rumours suggesting a launch as early as 2027, Apple has never responded to such speculation. However, Apple quietly filed a patent application for a "six-sided glass enclosure" back in 2019. Jefferies had previously considered an all-glass iPhone to be feasible, but Lee believes that development work has come to a standstill. According to the analyst, supply-chain checks indicate that the project was cancelled due to low yields. Lee considers this decision "a significant setback for pushing out a higher-priced iPhone amid surging memory prices." Had the device launched on schedule in September 2027 to mark the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, he estimated the blended retail price would reach US$2,060, higher than the average selling price of any model to date. Lee wrote: "More importantly, we believe the original plan was to extend the all-glass design to future iPhone Pro and Pro Max models, further boosting their average selling prices and profits." He believes that amid rising memory prices, this move should have served as an important defensive strategy.

Lee also pointed to Apple's artificial intelligence strategy and rising component costs for the iPhone 19 Pro as reasons for the further downgrade of the company's stock rating.

From Lee's report, it is not entirely clear whether the analyst believes the entire redesign plan has been shelved, or merely that certain elements of it have been cancelled.

Top-rated comment by Currentinterest

These analysts have repeatedly been wrong in their predictions about Apple's future plans in the past. The term "all-glass" may never have accurately reflected what Apple truly intends to do. The 20th-anniversary handset will feature an innovative design, and regardless of the final design, the market will demand it.

For example, rumours have long suggested that Apple will be unable to completely eliminate the Dynamic Island cutout next year. Therefore, an "all-glass" display is simply impossible to achieve. However, the rumoured four-curved-edge design could still potentially launch.

In any case, if Apple's iPhone 20th-anniversary design has truly been cancelled, we should receive confirmation from other reliable sources very soon.

What are your thoughts on this report about the iPhone 20th-anniversary design? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
